description: A heavy metal chemical element with atomic number 82 and symbol Pb, characterized by its soft, malleable nature and relatively low melting point. It appears shiny silvery with a bluish tint when freshly cut or melted, but tarnishes to dull gray on exposure to air. Lead is the highest atomic number of any stable element, with three of its isotopes serving as endpoints of major nuclear decay chains.
uses: Lead has been extensively used since ancient times in construction, plumbing, batteries, bullets, shots, weights, solders, pewter, fusible alloys, lead paints, leaded gasoline, and radiation shielding. It played a crucial role in the development of the printing press, as movable type could be relatively easily cast from lead alloys. In 2022, about twelve million tonnes of lead were produced globally, with two-thirds coming from recycling.
characteristics: Lead is characterized by high density (11.34 g/cm³), malleability, ductility, and resistance to corrosion due to passivation. It is soft with a Mohs hardness of 1.5 and melts at 327.5 °C, making it one of the lowest melting points among metals. It becomes a superconductor below 7.19 K and is a neurotoxin that accumulates in soft tissues and bones, damaging the nervous system and interfering with biological enzymes.
